question: What is the primary site of sperm production within the testes?
explanation: Spermatogenesis takes place continuously inside the microscopic seminiferous tubules of the testes. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which cells are responsible for testosterone synthesis in the testes?
explanation: Interstitial cells of Leydig located between the tubules produce and secrete testosterone. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which hormone directly stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone?
explanation: Luteinizing hormone travels from the anterior pituitary to bind Leydig cells and promote testosterone synthesis. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary function of inhibin in the male reproductive system?

options.B: Enhancing androgen receptor binding in target tissues
options.D: Directly inducing spermatogenesis in the epididymis

explanation: Inhibin is released by Sertoli cells to provide negative feedback specifically targeting pituitary release of follicle-stimulating hormone. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h2)

question: What pathological event occurs during testicular torsion?
explanation: Testicular torsion happens when the spermatic cord twists, shutting off arterial blood flow and venous drainage. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why does acute orchitis cause severe, intense pain within the scrotum?

options.A: Swelling is restricted by the tight tunica albuginea
options.B: Bacterial toxins directly destroy sensory nerve endings
options.C: Ischemia damages the surrounding scrotal skin layers
options.D: Venous congestion triggers systemic inflammatory cytokines

explanation: The tough outer capsule of the testis prevents easy expansion, causing high internal pressure and severe pain when inflammation causes swelling. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why is a varicocele much more common on the left side?

options.A: The left testis is anatomically larger and heavier than the right testis
options.B: Bacterial reflux occurs more frequently from the left ureter
options.C: Increased gravitational pull affects the left side of the scrotal sac
options.D: The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein at a right angle

explanation: The anatomical pathway of the left testicular vein creates higher resistance and pressure compared to the right vein draining directly into the vena cava. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h4)

question: How does a varicocele negatively impact male fertility?

options.A: By destroying circulating testosterone molecules in the blood
options.B: By obstructing the vas deferens and preventing sperm transit
options.C: By increasing scrotal temperature and impairing spermatogenesis
options.D: By triggering autoimmune attacks against mature spermatozoa

explanation: Venous pooling raises local scrotal temperature above the optimal level required for healthy sperm production. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h4)

question: In which part of the prostate does benign prostatic hyperplasia typically begin?
explanation: Benign prostatic hyperplasia specifically originates in the transition zone surrounding the urethra, leading to early urethral compression and urinary symptoms. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is a major clinical consequence of chronic, untreated urethral obstruction caused by prostate enlargement?

options.A: Bladder hypertrophy and residual urine accumulation
options.D: Atrophy of the bilateral adrenal glands

explanation: The bladder works harder to push urine past the narrowed urethra, causing muscle thickening, loss of tone, and incomplete emptying. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which genetic condition is a common primary testicular cause of male infertility?
explanation: Klinefelter syndrome involves an extra X chromosome (4XXY), causing primary testicular failure and small, firm testes. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h6)

question: What classifies a case of male infertility as post-testicular?

options.A: Systemic autoimmune destruction of circulating testosterone
options.B: Genetic destruction of germ cells within the seminiferous tubules
options.C: Inadequate hormone signaling from the anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Obstruction or functional defect in the sperm transport ducts

explanation: Post-testicular infertility occurs when sperm are produced successfully but cannot be transported due to blockages or structural defects in the ducts. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h6)

question: What parameter is primarily evaluated during a standard semen analysis for fertility?

options.A: Prostate-specific antigen and prostatic acid phosphatase
options.B: Serum testosterone and luteinizing hormone levels
options.D: Bacterial load and white blood cell density

explanation: Semen analysis measures the physical and functional characteristics of ejaculated sperm, including count, movement, and shape. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h7)

question: Why is a scrotal ultrasound ordered when evaluating acute scrotal pain?

options.A: To measure systemic levels of circulating gonadotropin hormones
options.B: To visualize the patency of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis
options.C: To confirm the presence of prostate-specific antigen in the blood
options.D: To differentiate between testicular torsion and inflammatory conditions

explanation: Ultrasound with Doppler flow allows clinicians to quickly assess blood flow to the testis, ruling out or confirming ischemia. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility immediately following a transurethral resection of the prostate?

options.A: Applying warm compresses directly to the perineal skin incision
options.B: Checking daily serum prostate-specific antigen levels every morning
options.C: Monitoring urinary catheter patency and continuous bladder irrigation
options.D: Administering high-dose testosterone injections to prevent fatigue

explanation: Continuous bladder irrigation keeps the catheter free of blood clots and prevents urinary retention following prostate surgery. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h8)

question: How should a nurse best support a patient newly diagnosed with testicular cancer?

options.A: Discouraging discussion about body image changes to maintain morale
options.B: Providing a supportive environment and facilitating counseling referrals
options.C: Focusing solely on physical wound care to avoid emotional distress
options.D: Assuring the patient that fertility is never affected by treatment

explanation: Open communication and professional psychological support help patients cope with the emotional impact of diagnosis and treatment. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h8)
